Customer feedback on citation reliability improved dramatically from Q1 to Q2 2026, moving from the top complaint category to a largely resolved issue. Specifically, citation accuracy was the single most prominent complaint in Q1 [NL-010#NL-010-S01], driven by incorrect file links (42%), missing page numbers (28%), empty citations (18%), and broken links (12%) [NL-010#NL-010-S05], which caused enterprise clients like BrightPath Healthcare to pause their clinical pilot [NL-010#NL-010-S05].

After the April 2026 fix (which bound document metadata to vector chunks at ingestion and added semantic chunking/re-ranking) [NL-011#NL-011-S05][NL-016#NL-016-S04], Q2 feedback shows a steady decline in citation-accuracy tickets—from 88 in March to 42 in April, 31 in May, and 24 in June [NL-011#NL-011-S05]. Users now report being directed to the exact section or page range, and trust improved in regulated industries, with BrightPath restarting their pilot [NL-011#NL-011-S03]. Overall NPS rose from 41 in Q1 to 44 in Q2 [NL-011#NL-011-S02][NL-011#NL-011-S01].

However, the trend is not fully resolved: remaining Q2 tickets are almost entirely linked to scanned, image-only PDFs where citation anchors cannot be established [NL-011#NL-011-S05][NL-016#NL-016-S04], and there is a minor lag in citation indexing during peak hours that causes temporary errors with older file versions [NL-011#NL-011-S05].
